families.signature: Overlapping pattern requirements can cause memory interference: an assembler may carry one pattern's count into another. Omissions should cluster at pattern transitions or shared materials, with the picked quantity matching a different pattern's requirement.
families.assumptions: Volunteers switch patterns and rely on memory. Five shared-material omissions are consistent with interference but could also reflect filling losses or shortages; transition and quantity records are absent.

families.signature: Shared-tray access can create movement contention. Cross-reaching should coincide with pauses, interrupted counts or material displacement, and kits assembled during those interruptions may take longer or contain more errors.
families.assumptions: The 38 reaches interfere with work rather than being harmless movement. The tally supplies no duration or kit-level linkage, so it cannot quantify delay or establish an omission cause.

families.signature: Local material visibility may reduce search and picking mistakes, but small-batch success may instead reflect an easier pattern mix or lower workload. Error and time differences should follow comparable patterns and quantities before being attributed to material placement.
families.assumptions: Loose materials are distinguishable and fit the table. Twelve kits provide limited exposure; their pattern mixture, preparation time and full-session feasibility are unknown.

families.signature: Visible stock depletion can mimic a true shortage when reserve supplies are hidden. Picking should pause or skip a required colour after the tray empties despite remaining usable inventory, with availability restored when the reserve is discovered.
families.assumptions: The unopened packet contains the required colour and dimensions. The record indicates usable sheets but does not connect depletion to omitted items or measure interruption time.

families.signature: Deferred checking creates a serial work tail and allows errors to accumulate before detection. Total readiness time exceeds filling time, and corrections discovered at the end can extend the tail further; repeated defects may span many completed envelopes.
families.assumptions: The eleven-minute check is additional elapsed work within the stipulated assembly window. Check staffing, correction time and detection completeness are unspecified; the contents audit may be separate from that check.

families.signature: An envelope's contents can be complete while its assigned pattern is unclear during distribution. Exchanges should arise from identity ambiguity rather than missing contents, with a correct kit initially reaching the wrong pattern recipient.
families.assumptions: Participants' assignments are stable and exchanges reflect exterior ambiguity. Three exchanges do not prove incomplete kits; their treatment as corrections under the success measure is unspecified.
